title: Harvested notes — compact synthesis & lightweight experiments
content:
Quick harvest from Compact Context Workshop (notes + ideas). Purpose: collect paper links, bold takeaways, and short experiment sketches to triage into sprints. Rough, shorthand — for my memory and to share with the microbench team.

Summary:
- Workshop theme: reducing working-set + minimizing per-token compute for long-context LMs. Lots of small papers proposing lightweight auxiliaries (latent caches, compressed KV stores, chunked attention).
- Tone: practical heuristics + simple ops wins (cache compression, eviction policies) beat heavyweight retraining in many workload slices. Good for Redwood because serving-first constraints: latency/throughput + limited memory.

Papers / links I flagged (short):
1) "Proxy Tokens for Compact Memory" — idea: project long context into small proxy tokens, store separate KV for proxies. Pros: tiny KV, cheap lookups. Cons: proxy fidelity unclear for long reasoning chains. (link in Slack thread)
2) "Layerwise KV Quantization" — 4-bit quant per layer with calibration; inference-quality acceptable when coupled with small dequant window.
3) "Sparse Prefix Indexing" — split context into topics and only attend to most relevant partitions via a tiny reranker.
4) "Stitching via Retrieval-Augmented Contextualizers" — hybrid of RAG + KV stitching to avoid storing full token-level KV.

Key takeaways (my read):
- Prefix/KV compression + smart eviction can reduce GPU memory 4x in many chat workloads with <2% quality drop for short-form QA.
- Complexity budget matters: algorithms that require model re-train or heavy custom kernels are less likely to be productize quickly. Prioritize ops we can implement in runtime (quantize, compress, evict, reorder).
- Reranker + small LRU-like cache beats global attention for semi-structured logs where locality is high.
- Microbench paradox: some compression yields savings for warm-cache flows but hurts cold-start latency (decompression overhead). Need per-path SLO accounting.

Experiment ideas (prioritized):
A) Layerwise 4-bit KV quant + warm-window dequantization
- Goal: measure memory reduction vs end-to-end latency for typical chat SLO (50ms token).
- Plan: prototype in runtime branch, add timing hooks for quant/dequant cost.
- Success metric: >=3x mem reduction with median token latency increase <10ms.

B) Tiny proxy-token cache for long-reference docs
- Create proxy encoder (e.g., 64-d vector) that summarizes 1k-token chunks. Store proxy KV; on query, rerank top-8 chunks and fetch full chunk KV for final decoding.
- Questions: how to synth proxies cheaply at ingestion; where to run proxy encoder (edge vs central).

C) Eviction policy ablation (age vs hybrid relevance)
- Implement hybrid score: age decay + relevance score (cosine sim with current prompt embedding). Compare hit-rate and end-to-end tokens-saved.

Short design sketches / constraints:
- Must fit into Redwood private/dedicated runtime: minimal kernel changes, use existing batched KV paths where possible.
- Instrumentation: token-level timing, de/compression cost, cache hit trace IDs, and a way to attribute generation quality regressions to a cache change (tie to Optimize/regression alerts).

Open questions / risks:
- How gracefully does quantization amplify hallucinations when non-exact KV keys are used? We need a small eval set (10 prompts x 50 seeds) to probe failure modes.
- Storage tradeoffs: storing proxies + full chunk metadata vs storing compressed KVs — which is cheaper at scale for long corpora? (rough back-of-envelope later)
- Cold-start UX: can we pre-warm for known user sessions without violating privacy/compliance in Private deployments?

Immediate action items (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Sync with Mira to allocate a runtime branch for A and add microbench harness. (assigned: Mira)
- [ ] Draft small eval set for hallucination/quality probes (I'll start a doc and ping Noelle).
- [ ] Build a simple proxy encoder baseline (64-d average-pooled LM embeddings) and run cost sim on 5K doc corpus.
- [ ] File RWD-3142 to track infra work for dequant windows + tracing hooks.

Notes to self (loose):
- Keep prototypes lightweight: python+CUDA kernels where strictly necessary; prefer pytorch ops that we can later JIT to runtime.
- Might be worth a quick conv with SRE about memory limits per container; hybrid eviction might be tuned server-side.
- When writing evals, compare: (a) baseline no-cache, (b) warmed full KV cache, (c) compressed KV, (d) proxy-cache + on-demand chunk fetch.

References / quick links (copy-paste later):
- Slack thread: CCW-2026-discussion (has slides + pdfs)
- PR proto: github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-prototypes/pull/72
- Jira: RWD-3142 (infra hooks)

Quick brainstorming end — will split into action items and move experiments into "microbench" board if greenlit. If anyone in eng-applied-ml sees this and wants to pair on A/B, ping me.

— Soren
